page.layout: One page of text, verse. Running head centred at top, page number top right. Verse block below, flush-left and indented lines. Below it: the signature "R.P.I.T." set right, then a woodcut ornament. Faint show-through from the other side lies below the text and is not transcribed.

l.i: Ille preces firmat decumanis fluctibus: ille
O bene, Neptuni præda ingens, classis Ibera,
Anglia, quid celeres promis statione paroness?
Ille tuus prædo præda fit Oceano.
Anglia, quid flammis fugientia vela fatigas?
Anglia chara Deo, tibi cæli exercitus omnis
Scilicet hoc pacto mergetur in æquore tandem

page.notes: Line 5: "promis statione paroness?" — the final s is printed as a long-s form, read as "paroness" with the question mark after it. The "promis" and "statione" letters are clear enough in the scan, but the word after "promis" is written with a long s and was copied as "statione". Line 6: "prædo" and "præda" are the printed forms as best read; the diphthong forms were not checked further. Line 12: a swash-like mark stands directly before "Angelicis" (a reference sign or ornament, not a letter). It was not transcribed as text. A mark of this kind is not a margin note. Woodcut ornament below the signature: a cherub's head between two horns of plenty, with festoon drapery and pendants. Not text. Faint show-through below the text (mirrored text from the other side of the leaf, including fragments such as "HISPANIA" and "I.I.B.") is not transcribed.
